structure: Part 1, Notification record: fields and validation, read at repos/trade-imports-animals-backend main 15ae53f (tag 0.91.0). Read in full: README.md; every domain type in src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/ that shapes the record (NotificationAggregate, NotificationBase, Notification, NotificationDto, SaveNotificationDto plus the ActorRequest it names, NotificationStatus, Origin, Commodity, CommodityComplement, Species, AnimalIdentifier, Transport, MeansOfTransport, Transporter, Address, ConsignmentParty, AdditionalDetails, ReferenceNumberGenerator); configuration/StrictLocalDateModule and LocalDateStringConverters; every class in exceptions/ (GlobalExceptionHandler and its six exception types: BadRequestException, ConflictException, NotFoundException, ServiceUnavailableException, OutboxWriteException, TradeImportsAnimalsBackendException); and the tests GlobalExceptionHandlerTest (22 tests), ReferenceNumberGeneratorTest, NotificationAggregateTest, LocalDateStringConvertersTest, OpenApiDateFormatTest and utils/NotificationTestData. Layout: the stored document (collection notification) is NotificationAggregate, whose identity and metadata (id, referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created, updated, submittedAt, expireAt) sit at the top and whose content sits in a nested Notification sub-object (fields from NotificationBase), beside an opaque fulfilments list and two hidden pre-amend snapshots. The inbound request is SaveNotificationDto {notification: NotificationDto, actor: ActorRequest}. Content sections, in source order: origin, commodity with complements, species and animal identifiers, reason for import, additional details, six consignment parties with literal addresses, CPH number, transport with means of transport and transporter, purpose in internal market, destination country, port of exit and exit date. Covered: every field and its type section by section; the only validation constraints (notification required, reference-number path pattern) and the absence of any constraint on content; the four status values; the reference-number format and generation; strict calendar dates, their string storage and their API schema formats; every error response GlobalExceptionHandler produces (status, title, type, detail, errors map, traceId, code) and its logging; and what README.md says. Three lookups outside the read list were made to place what the slice names: NotificationController (the @Validated class, @Valid request bodies and the nine path variables carrying the reference-number pattern), ActorRequest, and application.yml's jackson write-dates-as-timestamps setting. What each endpoint does with the record is left to parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection named "notification".

The stored notification holds its identity and metadata at the top level and its content (parties, commodity, transport and so on) as a nested notification sub-object, beside a separate fulfilments payload.
claims.quote: Aggregate root: identity + metadata at the top, with the well-structured content held as a composed {@link Notification} sub-object (symmetric with the opaque {@link #fulfilments} payload).

claims.statement: Each stored notification has a string id as its database identity.
A notification's reference number is unique across all notifications, and the unique index is sparse, so notifications without a reference number are allowed and do not clash with each other.
claims.quote:
@Indexed(unique = true, sparse = true)
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a concurrencyToken that is the record's optimistic-locking version number.
Each notification carries a status, one of the NotificationStatus values.
Each notification records when it was created and when it was last updated, as instants (moments in time), stamped by the server.
claims.quote:
private Instant created;

    private Instant updated;

claims.statement: A client cannot set a notification's created or updated time: the request shape has no such fields and the server would discard them.
claims.quote: the aggregate's server-stamped {@code created}/{@code updated} instants are deliberately absent here; a client cannot set them and the server would discard them.

claims.statement: Each notification records submittedAt, the time of its most recent submission: set the first time it is submitted from DRAFT and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.
claims.quote: Timestamp of the most recent submission — set the first time the notification is submitted (from DRAFT) and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.

claims.statement: Starting an amendment or cancelling one leaves submittedAt unchanged, so it always points at the latest submission rather than the original one.
claims.quote: Left unchanged by amend and cancel-amend, so it always points at the latest submission event rather than the original one. Set by {@code submitNotification}; carried into the fulfilment-view projection.

claims.statement: A notification created through the app in a non-production environment carries an expiry time (expireAt), anchored to its created time, after which it becomes eligible for automatic expiry.
claims.quote: When this notification becomes eligible for automatic expiry, anchored to {@code created}. Set only for app-created notifications in non-prod environments

claims.statement: In production, and for notifications created before the expiry field existed, a notification has no expiry time.
claims.quote: {@code null} in prod and for notifications created before this field existed.

claims.statement: Expiry is driven by a sweep over a plain index rather than a database TTL index, so expiring a notification can also remove its accompanying documents.
claims.quote: Backed by a plain index (not a Mongo TTL index) so the expiry sweep can cascade to accompanying documents.

claims.statement: The expiry time is never shown in any JSON response.
Each notification stores a fulfilments payload (a list of documents recording obligation fulfilment) exactly as sent, byte for byte; the backend never interprets it.
claims.quote: Opaque obligation-fulfilment payload — persisted byte-faithfully; never interpreted by the backend.

claims.statement: When an amendment starts, the notification's content is snapshotted as it stood (including inline party details); cancelling the amendment restores that snapshot, and submitting the amendment clears it.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #notification}. Amend-only scratchpad: captured when an amendment starts, restored by cancel-amend, and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of {@link #preAmendFulfilments}; carries inline party details as they stood when the trader opened the amendment.

claims.statement: The fulfilments payload is snapshotted separately when an amendment starts, restored by cancelling the amendment and cleared when it is submitted, independently of the content snapshot.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #fulfilments}. Amend-only scratchpad: restored by cancel-amend and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of the content freeze.

claims.statement: Neither pre-amendment snapshot is ever shown in a JSON response.

Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once with an error rather than carrying on; the unexpected-error handler would turn that into a 500 response.
claims.quote:
return requireNonNull(notification,
            "NotificationAggregate requires a notification sub-object at this seam");
claims.note: Inferred that the failure reaches a caller as 500: a NullPointerException is a RuntimeException, which GlobalExceptionHandler.handleException maps to 500. Which endpoints reach this seam is parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A request to save a notification has a body with a notification object, which is required, and an optional actor object.
A save request without a notification object is rejected with a 400 validation error naming the notification field.
claims.note: Inferred from @NotNull together with the MethodArgumentNotValidException handler. NotificationController applies @Valid to the SaveNotificationDto body at lines 52 (POST /notifications) and 71 (PUT by reference number); which endpoints those are is parts 2 and 3. The message would be the Bean Validation default ("must not be null").

claims.statement: The actor on a save request identifies who made the change: an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and the organisation id acted on behalf of; it is passed on as the actor of the change.
claims.note: ActorRequest is not in this part's read list; it was read because SaveNotificationDto names it. Where the actor goes (the outbox Actor) is part 5.

claims.statement: The notification object in a request carries the content fields plus referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken and the fulfilments payload.
The request shape is only ever inbound: no endpoint returns it; every endpoint returns the stored notification or one of its view projections.
claims.quote: It is never a response body — every endpoint returns {@link NotificationAggregate} or one of the view projections

claims.statement: The request shape is also the internal carrier the copy feature uses to create a new notification from an existing one.
claims.quote: Inbound request shape: the {@code notification} member of {@link SaveNotificationDto}, and the internal carrier {@link NotificationCopyMapper} hands to the create path.

claims.statement: No content field of the notification carries a validation constraint: the backend accepts any section or field missing or empty, with no required fields, lengths or formats enforced on the content.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/NotificationBase.java:12-50 and the section types Origin, Commodity, CommodityComplement, Species, AnimalIdentifier, Transport, Transporter, Address, ConsignmentParty, AdditionalDetails
claims.note: Inferred from absence: grep for jakarta.validation.constraints across src/main/java finds it only in SaveNotificationDto, NotificationController, DocumentUploadRequest and configuration classes; no domain type in notification/ has a constraint, so the cascading @Valid on notification has nothing to check.

claims.statement: The backend records no rule for which fields a notification must have before it can be submitted, nor any length or format rule for free-text fields such as the CPH number, email, phone or postcode.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/ (every domain type read in this part)
claims.note: Looked in every domain type in this slice and in GlobalExceptionHandler. Whether submit checks completeness in the service is part 2's to say.

claims.statement: The same content fields are shared by the stored content sub-object and the request shape.
claims.quote: Shared content fields extended by {@link Notification} (content sub-object) and {@link NotificationDto} (wire type).

claims.statement: A notification's content includes an origin section.
The origin section records the country of origin as a code (countryCode).
The origin section records whether a region code is required (requiresRegionCode), held as a string rather than a boolean.
The origin section records the trader's own internal reference (internalReference).
The origin section records a region of origin code (regionOfOriginCode).
The origin section records a country subdivision code (countrySubdivisionCode).
A notification's content includes a commodity section.
The commodity section records a commodity name.
The commodity section holds a list of commodity complements, so one notification can carry more than one commodity line.
Each commodity complement records a type of commodity as free text.
Each commodity complement records the total number of animals as a whole number.
Each commodity complement records the total number of packages as a whole number.
Each commodity complement holds a list of species lines.
A species line records the species as a code (value) and its display name (text), for example BOV and Bovine.
claims.quote:
private String value;
    private String text;
claims.note: The BOV/Bovine example is test data (.value("BOV") .text("Bovine")), not a code list.

claims.statement: A species line records its number of animals as a whole number.
A species line records its number of packages as a whole number.
A species line has single ear tag, passport and microchip fields of its own, alongside its list of animal identifiers.
claims.note: The record holds identifiers in two places: these single line-level fields and the per-animal list (claim repo-backend-p1-046). The source does not say which one is current.

claims.statement: A species line holds a list of animal identifiers, one entry for every animal unit on the line, not only the first.
claims.quote: One animal-identifier unit on a {@link Species} line — every unit, not just the first.

claims.statement: An animal identifier entry records a microchip number.
An animal identifier entry records a passport number.
An animal identifier entry records a tattoo.
An animal identifier entry records an ear tag.
An animal identifier entry records a horse name.
An animal identifier entry records a permanent address as a full party (name, email, phone and address).
A notification's content records a reason for import as free text.
A notification's content includes an additional details section.
Additional details record what the animals are certified for (certifiedFor), as free text.
Additional details record whether there are unweaned animals, held as a string rather than a boolean.
A notification's content records six parties: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, destination and consignment contact.
claims.quote: A party on a notification — consignor, consignee, importer, place of origin, destination or the consignment contact.

claims.statement: Each party on a notification records a name.
Each party on a notification records an email address.
Each party on a notification records a phone number.
Each party on a notification records an address.
A party is held on the notification as a literal copy of the address the trader picked, so later edits to or deletions from the address book never change the notification.
claims.quote: Held as a literal copy of the address the trader picked: later edits or deletions in the address book never reach the notification.

claims.statement: An address is a Standard Address Block of address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode and country code.
claims.note: The class comment calls this "A Standard Address Block."

claims.statement: An address's field names follow the address book, the system of record for saved addresses, so a record copied from it maps across without translation.
claims.quote: Field names follow the address book (the system of record for saved addresses), so a record copied from it maps across without translation.

claims.statement: An address records its country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, not a display name.
claims.quote: {@code countryCode} is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (cv-011), not a display name.
claims.note: cv-011 is cited as the source of this rule; the code does not check the value is a real alpha-2 code.

claims.statement: The address shape no longer has an address line 3, a city field or a free-text country: those were replaced by the address-book shape.
claims.quote: This replaced an earlier shape carrying {@code addressLine3}, {@code city} and a free-text {@code country}

claims.statement: A notification's content records a CPH (county parish holding) number as free text.
A notification's content includes a transport section.
The transport section records the port of entry.
The transport section records the arrival date as a calendar date with no time or zone.
claims.quote:
/** The chosen arrival day, as a calendar date. See {@link NotificationBase#exitDate}. */
    private LocalDate arrivalDate;

claims.statement: The transport section records the means of transport.
The means of transport is one of four values: AIRPLANE (Airplane), RAILWAY (Railway), ROAD_VEHICLE (Road vehicle) or VESSEL (Vessel).
A means of transport outside the four listed values cannot be stored: it does not fit the field's type, so the request body is rejected as malformed with a 400.
claims.quote: Handle an unparseable request body (400 Bad Request) — malformed JSON, or a value that does not fit the field's type.
claims.note: Inferred: an unknown enum constant fails JSON binding (HttpMessageNotReadableException), which the handler maps to 400 Malformed Request. Assumes Jackson's default of failing on unknown enum values; no override was seen.

claims.statement: The transport section records the transport identification (for example a vehicle registration or flight number).
claims.note: The examples are the extractor's reading of the field name; the source gives none.

claims.statement: The transport section records a transport document reference.
The transport section records a list of countries the consignment transits.
The transport section records one transporter.
A transporter records a name, an address, an approval number and a type.
A transporter's type is free text; the test data uses "Commercial" and "Private", and approval numbers such as "ES-T2-45001294", "DE/BURY/T2/00104115" and "UK/BURY/T2/00104115".
claims.note: Inferred from test fixtures only: the type field is a plain String with no code list.

claims.statement: A transporter has no email or phone, unlike the other parties.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing Transporter with ConsignmentParty.

claims.statement: A notification's content records a purpose in the internal market as free text.
A notification's content records a destination country.
A notification's content records a port of exit.
A notification's content records an exit date: the calendar day the user chose, with no time and no zone, so no reader can shift it by a day.
claims.quote: A calendar day the user chose, carried as a {@code LocalDate}: {@code YYYY-MM-DD} on the wire and a string in Mongo. It has no time and no zone, so no reader can shift it by a day.

claims.statement: DRAFT is one of the notification status values.
SUBMITTED is one of the notification status values.
AMEND is one of the notification status values, for a submitted notification being amended.
DELETED is one of the notification status values, so a deleted notification can remain as a record with that status.
claims.note: The value is verbatim; that deletion is a status change rather than removal is inferred from its existence and is for part 3 to confirm.

claims.statement: There are exactly four notification statuses; there is no status for cancelled, rejected, in-progress or a template.
A notification reference number has the format GBN-AG-{YY}-{XXXXXX}.
claims.quote: Generates notification reference numbers in the format {@code GBN-AG-{YY}-{XXXXXX}}.

claims.statement: The YY part of a reference number is the last two digits of the current year when it is generated, zero-padded.
The last part of a reference number is 6 random Crockford base32 characters: digits 0 to 9 and letters A to Z except I, L, O and U.
claims.quote: {@code XXXXXX} is a 6-character Crockford base32 random body (digits 0–9 and letters A–Z excluding I, L, O, U), drawn from {@link SecureRandom}.

claims.statement: Reference numbers are random, drawn from a cryptographically secure source, not sequential.
claims.quote: private static final SecureRandom SECURE_RANDOM = new SecureRandom();

claims.statement: The generator does not itself guarantee a reference number is new: detecting a collision and retrying when saving fails is left to whatever calls it.
claims.quote: Collision detection and retry on persistence failure are handled by the caller.

claims.statement: A reference number given in a request path must match ^GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$; one that does not is rejected with a 400 validation error.
claims.note: NotificationController is outside this part's read list; it is @Validated (line 38) and a grep showed the pattern on the referenceNumber path variable of nine endpoints (lines 70, 89, 113, 132, 150, 182, 207, 223, 241). Which endpoints those are is parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A reference number that fails the path pattern gets the error message must match "^GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$" under the field name referenceNumber.
claims.note: The message is the Bean Validation default for @Pattern, as the unit test mocks it.

claims.statement: Date-only fields such as the arrival date and the exit date accept only a plain calendar date in the form YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-07-21.
claims.quote: Makes JSON binding of every {@link LocalDate} strict, so a date-only field accepts {@code 2026-07-21} and nothing else.

claims.statement: A date-only field sent as a date-time, such as 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z or 2026-07-21T00:00:00, is rejected with a 400 rather than having its time part silently dropped.
claims.quote: Jackson's {@code LocalDateDeserializer} is lenient by default: handed {@code 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z} or {@code 2026-07-21T00:00:00} it keeps the date part and drops the rest. A caller that sends a moment where a calendar date belongs would then be told 200, and the day it meant would depend on a zone nobody stated. With leniency off the value fails to parse and the caller gets 400.

claims.statement: The strict-date rule applies to every date-only field, including any added in future, because it is set for the date type rather than field by field; timestamp fields are not affected.
claims.quote: The override is set for the type rather than with {@code @JsonFormat} on each field, so a future {@code LocalDate} field cannot forget it. {@code Instant} binding is untouched.

claims.statement: A timestamp sent where a date-only value is required, or a date-only value where a timestamp is required, is rejected with a 400 Malformed Request rather than a 500.
claims.quote: Dates make that reachable in an ordinary way: a date-only field is a {@code LocalDate} and a timestamp is an {@code Instant}, so {@code "2026-12-12T00:00:00Z"} where {@code "2026-12-12"} is required, or the reverse, lands here rather than binding.

claims.statement: Calendar dates are stored in the database as ISO-8601 strings (for example "2026-07-21"), not as database date values, so they read back as the same date on any host whatever its time zone.
claims.quote: These converters store the date as its ISO-8601 string, {@code 2026-07-21}, so no zone takes part in either direction and the value reads back as the same date on any host.

claims.statement: Storing dates as strings fixed a bug (EUDPA-282) where, under UK summer time, a calendar date was stored as the previous day.
claims.quote: under {@code Europe/London} during BST, {@code 2026-07-21} lands on {@code 2026-07-20T23:00:00Z}, a calendar day early (EUDPA-282).

claims.statement: Because stored calendar dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings, sorting and range queries on them work in date order.
claims.quote: {@code YYYY-MM-DD} strings sort in date order, so sorts and range queries on these fields work as string comparisons.

claims.statement: Moments in time (created, updated, submittedAt) are timestamps and are not stored as strings; only date-only fields are.
claims.quote: Moments use {@link java.time.Instant}, which needs no custom converter.

claims.statement: The published API schema describes arrivalDate, exitDate and dateOfIssue as format date, and created, updated and submittedAt as format date-time, wherever they appear in a request or response.
claims.quote:
"arrivalDate, date",
        "exitDate, date",
        "dateOfIssue, date",
        "created, date-time",
        "updated, date-time",
        "submittedAt, date-time"
claims.note: dateOfIssue belongs to accompanying documents (part 4); it is listed here because this test holds it to the same rule.

claims.statement: Dates and timestamps are returned as ISO-8601 strings, never as epoch numbers or [year, month, day] arrays.
claims.quote:
# Timestamps on this API are Instants and date-only fields are LocalDates. Enabling this
      # would serialise an Instant as a decimal epoch and a LocalDate as a [year, month, day]
      # array instead of ISO-8601 strings — a silent contract break. Pinned to the Spring Boot
      # default so it cannot change by accident.
      write-dates-as-timestamps: false
claims.note: application.yml is outside this part's read list; this one setting was read because it governs the date handling in scope.

claims.statement: Every error response is an RFC 7807 problem detail with content type application/problem+json.
claims.quote: Global exception handler producing RFC 7807 ProblemDetail responses with trace IDs.

claims.statement: An error response carries a traceId property when the request has a trace id, and leaves it out when it has none.
A request body that fails field validation gets 400 with title "Validation Error", detail "Validation failed for one or more fields" and type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/validation-error.
A field-validation error response carries an errors map from each failing field's name to the list of its messages.

A request parameter that fails validation (such as a malformed reference number in the path) gets the same 400 Validation Error response, with the errors map keyed by the parameter's own name rather than its full path.

A request body that cannot be read (malformed JSON, or a value that does not fit its field's type) gets 400 with title "Malformed Request" and type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/malformed-request.

The malformed-request detail reads: "Request body could not be read. Check the JSON is well-formed, that each date-only field is a date, for example 2026-12-12, and that each timestamp is an RFC 3339 instant, for example 2026-12-12T00:00:00Z".
claims.quote:
"Request body could not be read. Check the JSON is well-formed, that each date-only "
                + "field is a date, for example 2026-12-12, and that each timestamp is an "
                + "RFC 3339 instant, for example 2026-12-12T00:00:00Z"

claims.statement: A malformed-request response has no errors map, because nothing was bound to name fields in.
claims.quote: A problem type of its own, not field validation: nothing bound, so there is no {@code errors} map to name fields in.

claims.statement: A malformed-request response never echoes the parser's message, which would quote the submitted value and name internal types; it is only logged.
claims.quote: The parser message is logged but deliberately not returned — it quotes the submitted value and names internal types.

claims.statement: An application-level bad request gets 400 with title "Bad Request", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request and the exception's own message as the detail.
claims.note: The test example detail is "Scan callback missing required correlationId in metadata" (a document-scan callback, part 4).

claims.statement: A request for something that does not exist gets 404 with title "Resource Not Found", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found and the exception's message as the detail.
claims.note: Test example detail: "NotificationAggregate with id 12345 not found". The real messages are thrown in parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A failure in an upstream service (unreachable, timed out or returning a non-2xx response) gets 502 with title "Upstream Service Error", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/upstream-error and the exception's message as the detail.
claims.quote: Exception thrown when an upstream service is unreachable, the connection times out, or the upstream service returns a non-2xx response. Will be mapped to 502 Bad Gateway by GlobalExceptionHandler.
claims.note: Test example detail: "cdp-uploader returned an error response: HTTP 503".

claims.statement: A resource conflict, such as a duplicate key, gets 409 with title "Resource Conflict", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/conflict and the exception's message as the detail.
claims.quote: Exception thrown when a resource conflict occurs (e.g., duplicate key). Will be mapped to 409 Conflict by GlobalExceptionHandler.
claims.note: Test example detail: "NotificationAggregate with reference GBN-AG-26-000001 already exists".

claims.statement: Saving a notification with a stale concurrency token (someone else changed it first) gets 409 with title "Stale Concurrency Token", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/stale-concurrency-token and a code property STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN.
The stale-concurrency-token detail reads: "The record was modified by another request; refresh and try again."
claims.quote: "The record was modified by another request; refresh and try again."

claims.statement: An upload larger than the permitted size gets 413 with title "Payload Too Large", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/payload-too-large and detail "Uploaded file exceeds the maximum permitted size".
claims.quote: "Uploaded file exceeds the maximum permitted size"

claims.statement: A failure writing the outbox event during submission gets 500 with title "Internal Server Error", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/internal-error and detail "An error occurred during submission. Please try again."
claims.quote: "An error occurred during submission. Please try again."
claims.note: The detail names submission whatever write raised the exception; which writes append an outbox event is parts 2 and 5.

claims.statement: An outbox-write failure response reveals no internal detail (such as lock keys, database error codes, stack traces, the aggregate id or reference number); full detail is logged on the server only.
claims.quote: Logs full diagnostic detail server-side; returns a generic message to the client so no internal details (lock keys, mongo error codes, stack traces) are leaked.

claims.statement: Any other unexpected application error gets 500 with title "Internal Server Error", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/internal-error and detail "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."
claims.quote: "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."

claims.statement: Framework-level HTTP errors, such as a request to an endpoint that does not exist, are left to Spring's own handling (for example 404) rather than becoming a 500.
claims.quote: Note: Does NOT catch Spring framework exceptions like NoResourceFoundException (404) or other HTTP-related exceptions. Only catches application-level exceptions.

claims.statement: README.md describes the service only as a core delivery Spring Boot backend template, and says nothing about the notification record, its API or any decision.
claims.quote: Core delivery Java Spring Boot backend template.
claims.note: README covers running the local stack, MongoDB, testing, running, SonarCloud, Dependabot and the licence. There is no CLAUDE.md and no rulings ledger in the repo.

claims.statement: The service stores its data in MongoDB, which CDP environments provide with credentials in environment variables.
claims.quote:
In CDP environments a MongoDB instance is already set up
and the credentials exposed as environment variables.

claims.statement: The repo owns the local Floci provisioning that creates the S3 buckets, SQS queues and the quarantine-bucket S3 event notification the service needs.
claims.quote:
[compose/start-floci.sh](compose/start-floci.sh) creates the S3
buckets, SQS queues, and the quarantine-bucket S3 event notification this
service needs.

claims.statement: The service will not start unless its own base URL (TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_BACKEND_BASE_URL) is set: a blank value fails startup with "must not be blank".
claims.quote:
`CdpConfig` enforces `@NotBlank` on it, so
startup fails fast with a binding/validation error
(`Property: cdp.backend.baseUrl`, `Reason: must not be blank`).

claims.statement: README says the tests run the full Spring Boot application against a containerised database and use no mocking of any sort.
claims.quote:
Tests run by running a full Spring Boot application backed by [Testcontainers](https://testcontainers.com/).
Tests do not use mocking of any sort and read and write from the containerized database.
claims.note: Not wholly true today: GlobalExceptionHandlerTest in this slice uses Mockito mocks. Recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: The service runs locally as part of the workspace stack, or on its own with only the database and infrastructure profiles (MongoDB, Floci, Redis).
claims.quote:
To run only the infrastructure this service needs rather than the full stack,
limit it to the `database` and `infrastructure` profiles (MongoDB, Floci,
Redis):

claims.statement: The calendar-date storage rule touches only typed date fields: a date-shaped string inside a plain text field or inside the untyped fulfilments payload is stored and read back unchanged.
claims.quote: The reader runs only where the target property is a {@code LocalDate}, so {@code String} fields and untyped payloads that happen to hold a date-shaped string are left alone.

claims.statement: Every error the handler answers is logged on the server with the request's trace id: client errors (validation, malformed body, bad request, not found, conflict, stale token, oversized upload) as warnings, and upstream, outbox-write and unexpected errors as errors.
A validation error response lists every failing field, and a field that fails more than one check carries each of its messages in its list, in the order the checks reported them.
claims.note: Inferred from the LinkedHashMap of lists: the unit test shows two fields (origin, commodity) each with one message; a field with several messages is the shape's reading, not a tested case.

claims.statement: Any party's address may be outside the UK: the test parties carry addresses with country codes CH, BE, GB, FR, IE and NO, and every test party has an email and a phone number.
claims.note: Inferred from test fixtures only; nothing in the record restricts an address's country.

claims.statement: The test data's species line fills the line-level identifiers as well as its counts: ear tag UK01234567890, passport UK0123456700999 and microchip 900123456789012 for 10 Bovine (BOV) animals in 5 packages.
claims.note: Test fixture only; it shows the single line-level identifier fields (claim repo-backend-p1-045) in use and leaves the animalIdentifiers list empty.

claims.statement: Application-level bad requests are for a payload that binds but which the application rejects, such as a callback missing required metadata.
claims.quote: Exception thrown when application-level validation rejects a request payload (for example, a callback payload missing required metadata). Mapped to 400 Bad Request by GlobalExceptionHandler.
